title: Fibre support bound for compactly supported higher direct images at finite coefficients
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring whose additive exponent is invertible in $k$. Use the ordinary derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated morphism of finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $d\ge0$ be an integer such that every scheme-theoretic fibre $X_y$, $y\in Y$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], has topological Krull dimension at most $d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $Rf_!$ be the compact-support direct image of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] and $R^qf_!=\mathcal H^qRf_!$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Let $F$ be a constructible sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] and $a\ge0$ an integer such that the closed support of a sheaf (the complement of the largest Zariski open on which it vanishes; by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] this is the closure of the set of points with a nonzero geometric stalk) $Z$ of $F$ has dimension at most $a$. Then for every integer $q$ the closed support of $R^qf_!F$ has dimension at most $a+d-q$, the empty set having dimension $-\infty$. In particular $R^qf_!F=0$ for $q<0$ and for $q>a+d$.

source.place: 4.2.4 (support estimate for the compact-support direct image along fibres of dimension <= d)

proof.text: Choose a compactification $f=rj$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ an open immersion and $r:\overline X\to Y$ proper [thm-nagata-compactification], so $Rf_!F=Rr_*(j_!F)$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. The sheaf $j_!F$ is constructible: keep the finitely many strata of $F$ and add the closed complement $\overline X\setminus X$, on which it is zero. The scheme $\overline X$ is of finite type over $k$, so $Rr_*$ preserves bounded constructibility [thm-dg-finite-type-constructibility]; hence every $R^qf_!F$ is constructible, and it is zero for $q<0$. For a constructible sheaf $G$ on the Noetherian scheme $Y$ the set $S(G)$ of points with a nonzero geometric stalk is a finite union of strata, so it is constructible; its closure is the closed support of $G$ [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], and the generic point of every irreducible component of that closure lies in $S(G)$.

proof.text: Let $y\in Y$ with a geometric point $\bar y$ over it, and write $X_{\bar y}\subset\overline X_{\bar y}$ for the fibres. Proper base change for $r$ along $\bar y\to Y$ [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring] and base change for extension by zero [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change] identify $(R^qf_!F)_{\bar y}$ with $H^q(\overline X_{\bar y},(j_!F)|_{\overline X_{\bar y}})$, the cohomology with compact support of $F|_{X_{\bar y}}$. Proper base change is a general theorem of etale cohomology (not a step of the trace formula or of Poincare duality).

proof.text: Put $Z_y=Z\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ and $e(y)=\dim Z_y\le\dim X_y\le d$. The restriction of $j_!F$ to $\overline X_{\bar y}$ vanishes off the closure $W$ of $Z_{\bar y}$. As $Z_{\bar y}$ is closed in the open $X_{\bar y}$, it is open and dense in $W$, so $\dim W=\dim Z_{\bar y}$, and $\dim Z_{\bar y}=e(y)$ by [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change]. The sheaf is pushed forward from $W$ [lem-kun-04ca], so its cohomology is that of a torsion sheaf on the finite-type $\kappa(\bar y)$-scheme $W$. The field $\kappa(\bar y)$ is separably closed, of torsion cohomological dimension $0$, so [thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd] gives vanishing in degrees $q>2\dim W$. Hence $(R^qf_!F)_{\bar y}=0$ whenever $Z_y$ is empty or $q>2e(y)$.

proof.text: Let $q\ge0$ and let $T$ be an irreducible component of the closed support of $R^qf_!F$, with generic point $t$. By Step 1, $t$ has a nonzero stalk, so Step 3 gives $q\le2e(t)\le2d$ and $Z_t\neq\varnothing$. Let $Z'$ be the closure in $Z$ of an irreducible component of $Z_t$ of dimension $e(t)$; it is an irreducible closed subset of $Z\times_YT$ dominating $T$, its generic point $\zeta$ lies over $t$, and its fibre over $t$ is irreducible with generic point $\zeta$ and dimension $e(t)$. Apply [lem-zl-irreducible-fibre-dimension-lower-bound] to $Z'\to Y$ (with the reduced structure): $\dim Z'=\dim T+r$, and the local fibre dimension equals $r$ on a dense open of $Z'$, which contains $\zeta$; so $r=e(t)$. Therefore $\dim T=\dim Z'-e(t)\le a-\lceil q/2\rceil$.

source.place: 4.2.4: dim f(Z) + fibre dimension <= dim Z, Kiehl--Weissauer III

proof.text: Since $q\le2d$ we have $\lfloor q/2\rfloor\le d$, hence $a-\lceil q/2\rceil=a-q+\lfloor q/2\rfloor\le a+d-q$. The closed support of $R^qf_!F$ is the finite union of its irreducible components, so its dimension is at most $a+d-q$. When $a+d-q<0$ no component can exist, as a nonempty space has dimension at least $0$, and $R^qf_!F=0$.
